name: Walmart Supercenter — Flagler Landings
location: South side of State Road 100, just west of BJ’s Wholesale · Palm Coast
size: 38.81 acres · Walmart Supercenter of 186,276 sq ft approved · about 242,000 sq ft at full buildout (future retail and a fuel station follow by separate applications)
developer: Flagler Pines Properties LLC (landowner) · Flagler Venture, LLC (applicant)

timeline.text: City Council annexes the property into Palm Coast at the applicant’s request.
timeline.source: City of Palm Coast agenda packet, Sept. 1, 2026

timeline.text: Technical Site Plan — Tier 3 (Application #6587) submitted for a big-box anchor tenant on ±38.81 acres.
timeline.source: City of Palm Coast agenda packet, Sept. 1, 2026

timeline.text: Planning & Land Development Regulation Board recommends approval with conditions, 5–0.
timeline.source: PLDRB minutes and approving resolution — City of Palm Coast

timeline.text: City Council approves the technical site plan 5–0, with conditions. The anchor is set at 186,276 sq ft; the ±55,172 sq ft of future retail and the ±1,618 sq ft fuel station move to separate applications.
timeline.source: City Council meeting record, Sept. 1, 2026

timeline.text: Council also approves the proportionate-share and impact-fee agreement 5–0 — a $4.1 million share toward SR-100 improvements, with corridor work required at Site Development Permit issuance.
timeline.source: City Council meeting record, Sept. 1, 2026

timeline.text: A Site Development Permit follows once the remaining staff conditions are resolved; the SR-100 traffic improvements must be operational before construction begins, and conditions must be satisfied before building permits.
timeline.source: Daytona Beach News-Journal, Sept. 4, 2026

sources.label: Palm Coast agenda center — Application #6587 packet, minutes and resolutions
Daytona Beach News-Journal — “Palm Coast OKs Walmart site pending road upgrades,” Sept. 4, 2026

name: Palm Coast YMCA — Town Center
size: About $14M facility · Olympic-size pool · 35-year lease at $1/year on city land

timeline.text: Palm Coast City Council approves the city’s $3.25M share, contingent on the School Board’s $3M share.
timeline.source: FlaglerLive, Nov. 2026

timeline.text: Flagler County School Board unanimously approves the 35-year lease and its $3M share — the project’s final approval hurdle.
timeline.source: FlaglerLive + The Observer, Nov. 18, 2026

timeline.text: Construction planning for the Town Center site — no construction start date on record yet.
timeline.source: Town Center — Future YMCA Site card, this site

name: Town Center Land Purchase
developer: City of Palm Coast (buyer) · Palm Coast Holdings/Allete (seller)

timeline.text: City Council approves the $17M purchase of 23 Town Center parcels, 4–1.
timeline.source: Palm Coast City Hall card, this site (FlaglerLive on the purchase)

timeline.text: Council approves an $11 million loan to pay for the purchase.
timeline.source: Palm Coast City Hall card, this site

timeline.text: The city closes on the 23 parcels — about 259 acres — settling its lawsuit with Palm Coast Holdings/Allete.
timeline.source: Palm Coast City Hall card, this site

name: Lakeview Estates — Former Matanzas Golf Course
location: 398 Lakeview Blvd, Palm Coast — the 280-acre former Matanzas golf course
size: 280 acres · 250 single-family homes · 250,000 sq ft of neighborhood commercial · an ~11-acre community park

timeline.text: Lakeview Estates approved on the former Matanzas golf course (up to 272 homes).
timeline.source: Lakeview Estates card, this site (Daytona Beach News-Journal)

timeline.text: City Council tables the comprehensive-plan and MPD amendments 4–1, pending arsenic soil testing and other items.
timeline.source: City Council meeting record, Sept. 1, 2026

timeline.text: Council approves the revised plans — 39 more homes (250 total), 250,000 sq ft of commercial on Tract 9 fronting US-1, and an ~11-acre park on Tract 8; buffers raised and a soil test for arsenic required.
timeline.source: Lakeview Estates card, this site (Daytona Beach News-Journal; city agenda packet)

name: Evolve Palm Coast — Phase 2
location: 11 Evolve Pkwy, Palm Coast — US-1 at Whiteview Pkwy
size: 96 apartments in four three-story buildings · 352 homes in total with Phase 1 (built and leasing)

timeline.text: The Planning & Land Development Regulation Board approves the Phase 2 Technical Site Plan (Application No. 6796), and the city issues the Development Order the same day.
timeline.source: City of Palm Coast PLDRB packet, Nov. 18, 2026 (item D.3)

timeline.text: Conditions before building: school-concurrency sign-off, a FEMA flood-map amendment ahead of the site permit, and recreation finished before anyone moves in. Construction start not yet announced.
timeline.source: City of Palm Coast PLDRB packet, Nov. 18, 2026

name: DC BLOX Cable Landing Station
size: 33,760 sq ft · U.S. landing station for Google’s Sol subsea cable (Spain–Azores–Bermuda–Florida)

timeline.text: Building permit issued.
timeline.source: City of Palm Coast

timeline.text: Under construction in Town Center. The Sol cable comes ashore at Flagler Beach and runs inland to this site; no second building has been submitted or approved.
timeline.source: City of Palm Coast

timeline.text: Expected operational.
timeline.source: DC BLOX (company), via City of Palm Coast

sources.label: City of Palm Coast — cable landing station page

name: Flagler Beach Pier Replacement
location: S Ocean Shore Blvd, Flagler Beach
size: New concrete pier · deck 28 ft above sea level · pylons driven 80–125 ft deep

timeline.text: The old pier closes; a concrete replacement follows.
timeline.source: Flagler Beach Pier card, this site

timeline.text: The new concrete pier is under construction — pylons driven 80–125 ft deep, deck rising 28 ft above the sea. Commission decision: no access charge for the first year or two; planned open hours 5 a.m.–10 p.m.
timeline.source: Flagler Beach Pier card, this site

timeline.text: Substantial completion targeted for January 2027, with a spring opening planned.
timeline.source: Flagler Beach Pier card, this site
